text:
kevin: :rotating_light: alert-orchestrator appears to be suppressing pages unexpectedly for alerts coming from inference-gateway. PD webhooks are returning 429 from the orchestrator, so PagerDuty didn't get pages for ~8m. Seeing customer reports of 503s and high tail latency. Investigating now.

samir (oncall): I'm on it, waking up. Can someone dump the orchestrator logs and the last config change?

maria (sre): grabbing logs. quick check: our alert-orch started returning 429s to PD at 03:11 UTC. looks like rate_window_ms got accidentally set to 60000 in the feature rollout last night — causing aggressive suppression during bursts. snippet from logs:```json
{"ts":"2026-03-15T03:11:05Z","svc":"alert-orch","msg":"rate-limit-window exceeded","window_ms":60000,"action":"suppress"}```

ellie (product): customers hitting inference-gateway 503s started around 03:07 UTC per support thread. product impact: realtime Gen API degraded for some premium accounts.

priya (infra): patch was rolled by rollout/alerts-v2 at 02:50 UTC. there was a default that accidentally set RATE_WINDOW_MS to 60000. pushing a hotfix to unset. I'll try a config flip.

kevin: if orchestrator is returning 429 to PD, incident-bot won't create incidents. can someone try to create a PD incident manually and confirm paging works?

pagerduty-bot: failed to deliver webhook to alert-orch: http 429 response. payload id=abc123

samir (oncall): I'm going to trigger a manual PD page right now (phone rung). If that doesn't land we escalate to the secondary oncall.

kevin: command to flip rate window to previous value (safe):
```bash
curl -X POST "https://infra-api.internal/v1/alert-orch/config" 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $INFRATOKEN" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"RATE_WINDOW_MS": 0}'
```

maria (sre): doing it now. applying config change -> server returned 200. verifying.

devops-bot: config update applied to alert-orch (alerts-v2). rolling restart initiated. rollout id=rollouts/alerts-v2-20260315-03:26

priya (infra): kubectl rollout restart deployment/alert-orch -n infra applied. watching pods...

kevin: incident-bot still didn't create an incident automatically. posting manual thread in #incidents and paging manually was required. we should confirm automation fallback behavior.

incident-bot: ERROR: failed to create incident card due to upstream 429 from alert-orch. retrying in 30s.

samir (oncall): got the manual page, oncall acknowledged. I'm triaging root cause and looking for anything that changed the config value.

maria (sre): pods restarted and new instances show rate_window_ms=0 in env. sending a synthetic alert to verify flow.

kevin: synthetic alert went through and PD webhook returned 200. manual page worked, automation still suppressed earlier due to the 429 loop.

ellie (product): customers in support thread are being notified. we should message impacted accounts and let them know we're mitigating.

priya (infra): quick note: the config was introduced by alerts-v2 rollout; the default came from a missing env in the templating step (helm values had RATE_WINDOW_MS: 60000 accidentally). I'll open a PR to validate that variable and add e2e check.

maria (sre): immediate mitigation: reverted rollout, applied RATE_WINDOW_MS=0, restarted pods. secondary mitigation: add a circuit-breaker so the orchestrator doesn't return 429 to PD — instead it should queue locally and return 202. filing follow-up ticket.

kevin: customer-impact summary for now: several premium accounts saw increased 503s for up to ~10 minutes; no data loss, but delayed incident paging; manual PD page required to reach oncall.

samir (oncall): for live mitigation we: 1) flipped config 2) restarted deploy 3) manually paged PD 4) left pager incident open for monitoring. I will stay on it until next handoff.

ellie (product): I'm drafting a short customer-facing note for those affected.

priya (infra): created PR #3245 to add templating validation and a helm unit test to prevent RATE_WINDOW_MS default leakage.

incident-bot: created incident PD-48712 (manually) and attached channel log.

kevin: next steps: postmortem scheduled, add unit test + templating guard, update alert-orch to degrade gracefully (queue vs 429), and improve incident-bot fallback to create a local incident record if upstream fails. Can someone own the follow-ups?

maria (sre): I'll own the postmortem and the alert-orch graceful-degrade ticket.

priya (infra): I'll own the helm validation PR and the rollout templating check.

samir (oncall): I'll handoff to the next oncall in 50 minutes with notes. marking thread as "monitoring" for now.

kevin: thanks everyone. update on status in 30m or sooner if anything changes. :thumbsup:
